correctness.rationale: For a shattered k-support, all-positive trace yields a decreasing grid antichain. Each support point must admit a comparable replacement while all other marked points remain, forcing a slack coordinate in at least one flanking gap. At most two marked points share an unoccupied row/column level, giving 5k<=2(m+n). Explicit four-label maximal-antichain witnesses on 2x3 (and its transpose), plus two-label 1x2 witnesses, are anti-diagonally block-concatenated using ceil(k/2) spare coordinate levels, and maximal extension cannot add excluded marked points since they are already blocked. This handles every integer m,n>=1; independent finite enumeration on 28 rectangles through 7x7 and local patterns agrees. Only the written proof establishes the infinite claim.

value.rationale: A natural combinatorial question left by the 2024 complete census of maximal antichains is how many cell-membership queries those objects can realize independently. A sharp universal exact formula and aspect-ratio transition answer that question for all rectangular products; in square grids the fraction of width attainable is asymptotically 4/5, while full width occurs at ratio n/m >= 3/2. The new two-points-for-one-slack structural lemma and universal 2x3 gadgets explain the exact threshold and support further analysis.
